central_unknown: Rain is forecast throughout Sunday at Interlagos, with the greatest chance in the early afternoon. Wet conditions could reshuffle qualifying and race results dramatically, favoring wet-weather specialists like Verstappen while adding DNF risk to rookies and unreliable cars.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: Strong consensus across ZachGP and FanAmp as the #1 captain. Won both wet races this season (Singapore, Malaysia). Won 3 of the last 4 races. Excellent record at Interlagos. P3 in both FP1 and FP2. ML from Las Vegas projected 25.9 exp pts, ppm 1.62, MEDIUM risk — expect similar or better numbers in wet Brazil conditions where Verstappen historically excels. ZachGP explicitly calls him 'the two-times option for Brazil' and the best asset in changeable conditions.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lando Norris
captains.reason: Only 4.2% ownership in Global League top 500. Won this race last season. McLaren brought significant upgrades to Interlagos. Topped FP1, strong in wet conditions. FanAmp highlights him as a huge differential. ZachGP is more cautious, suspecting McLaren showed more pace than they actually have. ML from Vegas had Norris at 20.3 exp pts, MEDIUM risk — solid floor but lower ceiling than VER/ANT. High-reward play if McLaren upgrades deliver.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Home GP — potential Driver of the Day. P8 in both FP1 and FP2. Budget-increasing asset. Best cheap B-tier option per ZachGP consensus. Audi car looked competitive in practice.

buy.name: Carlos Sainz
buy.note: Strong recent form, consistent top-10 finisher. Needs only 2 points for minimum price increase. ZachGP moved him off the avoid list and into usable range. Williams looked decent in FP sessions despite some FP1 issues.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Veteran trusted in mixed/wet conditions per FanAmp. Key concern: Freddy Slater had reliability issues in HUL's car during FP1 — monitor whether Audi takes an engine penalty. If car is healthy, strong buy; if penalty or reliability doubt, downgrade to avoid.

consider.name: Pierre Gasly
consider.note: FanAmp trusts him in mixed conditions. Alpine finished P7 and P9 in FP1 even with Mini in Gasly's seat. Less FP running than others — monitor FP3.

consider.name: Alex Albon
consider.note: FanAmp warming to Williams duo. Williams had FP1 issues but Interlagos has strong overtaking opportunities. Decent wet-weather driver.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Racing Bulls showed decent Ferrari-powered pace in recent races. Budget-friendly option with potential price rise. BoxBox previously flagged him as a viable B-tier pick.

consider.name: Oliver Bearman
consider.note: Ferrari power unit advantage at Interlagos. Budget option but less upside than Bortoleto at similar price.

avoid: Raphael Camara — F1 debut in potentially wet conditions at a track he's never raced. Betting lines have him among top candidates for first retirement. Too risky despite home GP narrative and 6.0M price.
Esteban Ocon — Inactive/dropped from Haas. Remove immediately if still in team (-25 pts per race).
Rio Hirakawa — Inactive driver. Remove immediately if still in team.
Lance Stroll — Only finished 2 of last 9 races. DNF magnet despite budget floor price.
Fernando Alonso — Serial DNFs. Aston Martin reliability remains terrible despite upgrades.
Valtteri Bottas — DNF after DNF. Budget floor trap.
Sergio Perez — Minimal data from FP sessions, consistently underperforming.
Jack Doohan / Alpine B-driver — Not showing enough pace relative to budget.
Oscar Piastri — Still looks lost in the McLaren. Gave up FP1 seat. Not enough upside vs. price.

George Russell — 5-place grid penalty for IC change. Recent finishes of P9, P8, P6 since Baku win. Upside capped around 20-25 pts per FanAmp. Better options exist at A-tier price. However, Mercedes constructor may benefit from his recovery drive.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: If you're stuck with multiple dead assets (Ocon, Hirakawa, Stroll, Bottas) and need 3+ moves to get to an optimal Verstappen/Antonelli + strong B-tier build, Wildcard is justified. Season is winding down with limited races remaining. ZachGP and FanAmp both emphasize clearing out inactive and floor-price assets urgently.

chips.name: 3x Captain
chips.reason: Strong weekend for Verstappen but wet-weather variance adds risk to a 3x play. Consider saving for a more predictable race or a sprint weekend where points ceiling is higher. BoxBox used 3x at Monza on Antonelli in a more predictable scenario.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: No sprint this weekend limits Limitless ceiling. Save for a sprint race or a weekend with clearer pace hierarchy and less weather variance.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Hold for post-qualifying adjustments at a future race. Could be useful if Verstappen takes a surprise engine penalty later in the season, or for Las Vegas/Abu Dhabi optimization.

chips.name: Autopilot
chips.reason: ZachGP notes Autopilot could be 'very juicy' here — in dry conditions Antonelli likely wins, in wet conditions Verstappen excels. Having both on your team with Autopilot could capture the best captain outcome regardless of weather. Consider if you have both VER and ANT in your lineup.

watch_items: Rain forecast for Sunday — monitor hourly updates from weather sources like Ralpho on X. Greatest chance of rain in early afternoon; F1 may adjust start time.

Hulkenberg's car reliability — Freddy Slater's car had issues in FP1 and couldn't run in FP2. If Audi needs an engine change, Hulkenberg could take a grid penalty (changes him from buy to avoid as driver, but may help if you need overtake points).

Verstappen engine penalty rumors — Max has hinted at a potential engine penalty in the latter part of the season. ZachGP thinks it won't happen in Brazil (especially in wet), but a small chance exists. Even with penalty, ZachGP says it makes him an even better fantasy asset.
McLaren upgrades performance — biggest upgrade package on the grid this weekend. FP1 showed promise for Norris. Need to verify if these are genuine 2026 performance gains or 2027 test components.
Raphael Camara's debut performance in FP3/Quali — if he shows surprising pace, reconsider, but consensus is to avoid.

Mercedes constructor vs Red Bull constructor — Russell's 5-place penalty gives him recovery upside that could swing the Mercedes constructor matchup. FanAmp comfortable giving up Red Bull's 0.3M price gain edge because Mercedes has better F1 Fantasy scoring profile.
Williams FP1 issues — both cars had problems. Monitor if resolved by qualifying.
arc: Brazil is the penultimate or near-final opportunity to make significant team restructuring moves before the season-ending flyaway races. Clearing inactive drivers (Ocon, Hirakawa) is now critical as the -25 penalty per race compounds. The wet weather at Interlagos creates variance that could shake up the standings — a big Verstappen captain score here could lock in ranking gains heading into Las Vegas, where ML already projects Antonelli and Verstappen as the top two assets. Budget builders who lock in rising assets like Bortoleto and Sainz now will have more flexibility for Las Vegas and the finale. If you're holding Wildcard, the window to use it is narrowing rapidly — Brazil or Las Vegas are likely your last high-impact opportunities.
